02 · RC.99 · CLUSTER

Replication moved. Issue #1170 is still open.

Three pull requests since rc.98 connect the Raft log to real index operations. They are progress on #1170, which is still open. A single node is unchanged: with no cluster handle, writes and search stay on the node that received them.

  • #2257 proposes index create, delete, mapping, and settings through the Raft log when a cluster handle is attached. The HTTP call succeeds after this node has applied the committed entry. A follower forwards to the leader.
  • #2271 puts one primary per member into that same create entry. Member ids are sorted, and shard 0 is on the first member, shard 1 on the second, and so on. GET, PUT, and POST of one document, and DELETE /{index}/_doc/{id}, run on that owner. A search of one concrete index asks every owner.
  • #2287 copies an acknowledged document write onto replicas before the caller is answered. index.number_of_replicas at create places those copies on the next members in the ring, wrapping, never on the primary, and capped at one less than the member count. An absent setting places zero replicas. The bytes live in a hidden index, .xerj_replica_{index}_{shard}, so a search fan-out does not count a document twice. A replica that does not confirm is HTTP 503 replica_not_acknowledged: the primary has the write. GET can read a replica when the primary's transport fails. There is no promotion. A later settings change stores the new number and leaves the copies where they are.

#2287 lists what #1170 still requires. There is no quorum and no wait_for_active_shards: the write waits for every placed replica. Changing number_of_replicas after create does not relocate or backfill. Writes still need the primary. _bulk, _update, update-by-query, and native /v1 ingest do not route or replicate. Search does not merge aggregations, suggest, collapse, rescore, profile, search_after, or scroll across owners. That request is a 400 when the index has more than one owner. Unscoped /_search, comma lists, and wildcards stay on the node that received them. Scores are per shard, and the fan-out window is capped at 10,000. There is no snapshot install: the server does not open FileRaftLog, so a restart drops the in-memory plan. Later writes are not routed, and replica bytes that are still on disk are not served. Health endpoints still describe the answering node.

03 · RC.99 · THE NODE

CPUs, memory, a stale lock, and a document that is too big

x86_64 binaries no longer require AVX2 (#2253, fixing #2161). The release baseline is x86-64-v2 (SSE4.2: Nehalem and later, Bulldozer and later). The HNSW eight-accumulator dot product is the kernel that was worth a wider build: it compiles an AVX2+FMA variant and selects it at runtime when the CPU has both features. The scalar compilation is bit-identical. Installers install on a CPU without AVX2. XERJ_SKIP_CPU_CHECK is gone. A CPU without SSE4.2 still cannot run the binary. Field report #2158 is an Intel Core i3-3110M, Ivy Bridge, which has no AVX2. #2178 had made the installers refuse that machine. #2253 replaces the refusal.

Semantic embeddings take less memory in the memtable (#2240, fixing #1940). A semantic_text vector was stored as a JSON array of numbers, and both memtables kept that tree until flush. It is now one xerj:f32: hex string. GET and _source expand it back to a number array on the page that is returned. kNN and HNSW read the same bits.

Memtable pressure drains instead of stalling a corpus index (#2244, fixing #2238). When the summed memtable is what rejects a write, a drain runs so indexing can make progress. A bulk the parent breaker has not accepted a single item from stops at 90 seconds.

A stale node.lock is reclaimed (#2246, fixing #2233). The data-directory lock is still the OS file lock, so a live process still blocks a second start and the error still names that PID. On Windows, LockFileEx can stay busy after the holder is gone. If the lock is busy and the PID recorded in the file is not running, the file is replaced and the log says reclaimed stale node.lock left by pid <pid> (process is not running). A PID that cannot be read or checked is left alone. --auto-port does not treat that stale lock as a reason to start on an empty sibling directory.

One oversized JSON document is skipped, and the rest of the file can still index (#2256, #1122). A single JSON document over 8 MiB is not indexed, so one file of 50 MB or more cannot abort the node during autoindex or _bulk. Autoindex streams a top-level array, or a top-level array of records inside a larger object, one element at a time, and skips only the values over the limit. The skip names the file. A bulk item over the limit is HTTP 413, and its neighbours still index. The ceiling is fixed. Files over 64 MiB are still not read; the skip says so. The same pull request drops a segment whose file is already gone, instead of failing every later _search with Segment … not found. A sibling segment that is still on disk stays readable. Object-store mode is unchanged: a catalogue whose bundle is missing still refuses to open.

04 · RC.99 · SEARCH, MCP, WINDOWS

Definitions, templates, counts, a dependency bump, two install paths

MCP xerj_def (#2166) is local definition lookup, the rest of #2080 after prefix support. It takes symbol, prefix or index, kind, lang, k from 1 to 50, and max_tokens. No match is a successful empty hit list. Invalid arguments are rejected before any HTTP request.

MCP xerj_search accepts prefix (#2137). {"prefix":"project","query":"retry policy"} searches project-*. The default with neither index nor prefix remains ax-*. #2235 resolves that prefix the way xerj autoindex stores it, so My_Proj searches my-proj-*. An empty prefix, a prefix that cannot name an index, or index and prefix together is rejected before HTTP.

Index templates apply semantic_text and index.default_pipeline (#2283, #2281). A matching template was stored, and a keyword field from it was mapped, but semantic_text was stored as object and the default pipeline was dropped, so the pipeline never ran. Create now merges the highest-priority matching template, including the body xerj autoindex sends and the first bulk or single-document write that auto-creates the index. Where the request and the template both set a field or a setting, the request wins.

POST /{index}/_count honours min_score (#2277). The handler rebuilt a size: 0 search from the query alone, so the threshold was dropped: _search with min_score could return 0 while _count with the same body returned every match. The single-index path and the multi-index, _all, comma, and alias paths set it on the request. A non-numeric value is the same 400 parse_exception that _search returns.

ctutils is 0.4.5 (#2268). cargo-audit failed on 0.4.2. RUSTSEC-2026-0385, published 2026-10-23, says Choice mask generation and 32-bit u128 comparisons before 0.4.4 can branch on secret values. The patched range starts at 0.4.4. Nothing in the workspace Cargo.toml files names ctutils. It is transitive, through digest 0.11, from the AWS SDK crates and pdf_oxide. The diff is engine/Cargo.lock only.

Windows has two install directories, and the docs name both (#2289, #2285). The installers were already doing what they were written to do. curl -fsSL https://xerj.org/get | sh, including Git Bash, MSYS, and Cygwin, puts xerj.exe in ~/.local/bin and does not edit PATH. irm https://xerj.org/get.ps1 | iex puts xerj.exe in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\xerj and adds that directory to the user PATH, unless XERJ_NO_PATH=1. The README, llms.txt, the install page, and xerj mcp --help had each described one of those paths as the Windows location. Installer behaviour is unchanged. Upgrade by re-running the installer you used.

Also in the commits since the rc.98 tag, from the changelog on main: xerj --help lists xerj hub next to xerj ask when the build has a hub signing key (#2282). SIGTERM and SIGINT keep the HTTP ports bound until the final memtable flush has finished; new requests in that window get 503, and /health/live stays 200. A killed xerj corpus index resumes that build's journal (#2239). A semantic query on a semantic_text field returns highlight fragments when the request asks for them (#1947). A JSON object made of several top-level arrays of records no longer wedges autoindex (#1856, #1978). _refresh gives up after engine.flush_admit_timeout_secs (default 120) and engine.flush_timeout_secs (default 300) instead of waiting forever (#1635).

05 · WHAT YOU MISSED · RC.98

rc.98, 21 October: the console token bug, and autoindex that estimates first

v1.0.0-rc.98 was tagged on 2026-10-21. Between the v1.0.0-rc.97 and v1.0.0-rc.98 tags, git log shows 141 commits. 127 of them name a pull request (the subject ends in (#N), or the commit is a merge commit). The other 14 do not. That is the "~120 pull requests" in this window, counted.

CVE-2026-97406. #2003, published with CERT VU#645818 on 2026-10-20. POST /_xerj-console/api/v1/auth/api-tokens accepted any authenticated session, and Authorization: Bearer <api token> was one. Holding one API token was enough to mint independent successors. Revoking the parent left them working, because nothing recorded a parent. An owner token could issue an invitation, which the caller redeemed in their own browser to enroll their own passkey. Creating and revoking API tokens, issuing invitations, deleting passkeys, and logout now require a passkey-backed browser session and return 403 for a bearer token. Ordinary console calls (/me, preferences, dashboards, and the other data routes) still accept bearer tokens.

Budget-aware xerj autoindex. #2102 counts the folder and estimates the index before hashing, against free space under the node's flood-stage watermark. --max-index-size can lower that budget. When the default plan does not fit, stdout is a JSON plan list and the process exits 4 until --yes takes the plan that fits or --plan names one. #2128 stops a reduced plan from deleting files that are already indexed. The run exits 4 and lists them. --drop-indexed is the confirmation that deletes them. That deletion came from #2102 and never shipped in a release. #2087 stops before the walk when the node's data volume is already at or over the flood-stage watermark (default 95%). The probe reads the node, GET /_cat/allocation?format=json. --dry-run is never refused for disk. #2006 adds --walk-only, which prints each top-level folder's file count and size, and which ignore rule would drop what, and does not hash or sniff. #2126 adds xerj autoindex remove and the MCP tool xerj_autoindex_remove. They list indices, catalog rows, doc counts, and sizes, and delete nothing without --yes, a y at the terminal, or confirm: true.

An exact phrase ranks the file that contains it. #1759. On 100 string literals taken from XERJ's own Rust sources, the file that contains the literal went from rank 1 on 16 queries to rank 1 on 91. The same run's identifier set stayed at 92 of 100. The harness is benchmarks/search-exact-phrase/README.md, dated 2026-10-18 in that file. One of the word-split symbol queries got worse, rank 5 to rank 6. The README records it.

The same window is also the 26-client agent table (#2109), the MCP registry manifest server.json and the MCPB bundle builder (#1922), the field-report footer honouring --disable-feedback and XERJ_DISABLE_FEEDBACK (#1907), language routing for a bare hub question (#2104), and xerj ask exiting 6 when the hub catalogue cannot be loaded (#1905). The changelog's rc.98 section is the full list, including the Elasticsearch validation and aggregation fixes.

06 · WHAT YOU MISSED · RC.97

rc.97 switched Corpus Hub v2 on

v1.0.0-rc.97 was tagged on 2026-10-19. It is the first release that ships Corpus Hub v2 with the hub signing key compiled in. #1505 sets that ed25519 public key. rc.96's notes say the previous build had no key, so xerj ask, xerj hub pull, and the MCP hub tools exited 5 and downloaded nothing. The feature post is Corpus Hub v2, dated 2026-10-19, and the measurements live there. The rc.97 changelog section still contains TODO markers for two gate counts. This post does not fill them in.

What that changelog states, apart from those markers: the client routes a question from the signed catalogue on this machine, a symbol question returns the definition, other questions return passages with file:line, and an ambiguous question lists candidates and exits 4. xerj ask pulls a pack on its own only when the pack is 50 MB or less, and never when the licence class is Excluded. The packs directory has a 4 GB budget. There is no hosted search client in that release. The MCP tools xerj_hub_find, xerj_hub_def, and xerj_hub_ask never download a pack and never fetch the catalogue (#1629). The default embedder on that path is lexical feature-hashing.

07 · RC.81 THROUGH RC.96

Sixteen tags, and no release post for any of them

rc.81 (2026-10-03) through rc.96 (2026-10-15) is sixteen tags. The changelog names the shape of several of them, and this paragraph stays with those names. rc.81 is the agent-intake release. rc.82 extends autoindex to man pages and real spreadsheet shapes; the changelog calls those extractor pull requests thomas-villani's first contributions. rc.83 is the corpus-hub hundred: the notes say 100 live, licence-reviewed corpora on hub.xerj.org (#1164). rc.84 is the window where cluster health, node counts, and corpus-index exit codes report what happened. rc.85 fixes a cluster-ring election that churned when a peer was dead, and corrects the clustering page so it describes the ring that existed then. Replication was still unshipped. That is the same open issue, #1170, that rc.99 moves and does not close. rc.86 adds a server-derived audit actor class. rc.87 coalesces bulk bodies across files. rc.89 publishes the guest eval-scars post. rc.91 publishes the exploit-hub eval. rc.95 indexes legacy .xls and .doc. rc.96 says, in the changelog's own sentence, that Corpus Hub v2 is not a feature of that release.

08 · WHERE XERJ IS AVAILABLE

Clients the repo documents, and the listings still to paste

Install is the binary. The README's supported-agents table names 26 MCP clients that can register xerj mcp as a local stdio server. DeepSeek Harness (dsh) is one of them: a Cordis patch at $DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml, inserting @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client. The README marks that row untested. The only row marked tested is OpenCode v2.1.2 on Windows, against xerj v1.0.0-rc.97, which answered initialize and tools/list. The other rows are transcribed from each client's own documentation. The table and the per-client snippets are in the README under Supported agents.

The repo ships an MCP registry manifest, server.json, name io.github.xerj-org/xerj, added in rc.98 by #1922 along with an MCPB bundle builder. In this tree the manifest's version is 1.0.0-rc.97, and the package URL points at xerj-mcp-1.0.0-rc.97.mcpb on that GitHub release. This post does not claim a public directory is serving a newer package than that file names.

Two skill files live in the repository. tools/xerj-code/SKILL.md is the reference-coding skill. docs/case-studies/wordpress-security-audit/skill/SKILL.md is the WordPress audit skill. They are files in the tree. This post does not describe either one as a listing on an external skill registry.

09 · UPGRADE

Install v1.0.0-rc.99

The installers download a GitHub release and check its SHA-256. Pin this release with XERJ_VERSION. On Linux, macOS, and Windows Git Bash, MSYS, and Cygwin:

$ curl -fsSL https://xerj.org/get | XERJ_VERSION=v1.0.0-rc.99 sh
$ export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
$ xerj --version

That sh installer writes ~/.local/bin (xerj.exe on Windows) and does not edit your shell profile. PowerShell writes a different directory and adds it to the user PATH. Open a new terminal after it:

> $env:XERJ_VERSION='v1.0.0-rc.99'; irm https://xerj.org/get.ps1 | iex

Re-run the installer you used last time. The two do not share a directory. xerj --version should print v1.0.0-rc.99. The longer matrix, the manual checksum block, and the musl-versus-gnu choice are on the install page.
